---
name: Language review
about: You speak one of the languages and something in its guide sounds wrong
title: "[language review] "
labels: language, help wanted
---

Thanks for checking. Native speakers are the only way these guides get good.

**Which language?**
<!-- For example: Tamil, Gujarati, Spanish -->

**Which file?**
<!-- For example: write-like-human/references/languages/tamil.md -->

**What sounds wrong?**
<!-- Quote the line, then say why. "Nobody says this", "too formal for a chat", "wrong word for Sri Lankan Tamil", and so on. -->

**What would a native speaker write instead?**
<!-- Your version. A short note on when to use it helps too. -->

**Where are you from, or which variety do you speak?** (optional)
<!-- Usage differs a lot by region, so this helps us keep both versions when they're both right. -->

- [ ] I used made-up examples, not real messages from real people.
- [ ] I'm happy for my suggestion to be used under the project's MIT license.

Prefer to fix it yourself? Edit the file and open a pull request. When the whole file has been reviewed, remove its "Help wanted" section in the same pull request.
